summary: A real-time deduction puzzle where all players simultaneously race to find the shortest path to move a target robot to its goal, with robots sliding until they hit a wall or another robot. It's less a game and more a shared puzzle-solving competition, prized for how it sharpens spatial reasoning under time pressure.
praised: Great for mixed-skill and mixed-age groups
criticised: Real-time format can intimidate slower thinkers
Not really a 'game' in the traditional sense—no hidden info or strategy across turns
Can be dominated by a few fast players

interaction.detail: All players stare at the same shared board and race to shout out the shortest solution first; there's no individual tableau at all, just a single communal puzzle everyone attacks at once.

win_criteria: Most points, one or two sources

scoring.why: Every point comes from the same single source: being first to correctly call and execute a minimal-move solution to the current robot-target puzzle.
scoring.how_you_win: Players simultaneously study the board and shout out how many moves they think it takes to route the target robot to its marked square; whoever finds a valid solution in the fewest moves claims the point, and the first to a set number of points (or most after a fixed number of puzzles) wins.
